objectives.description: Classify each failing suite as CONSISTENT-FAIL or INTERMITTENT vs research's list
objectives.note: 4 CONSISTENT-FAIL matching research exactly: test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh, test-orchestrate-context-growth.sh, test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh, test-orchestrate-recover-message-findings.sh. 1 INTERMITTENT matching research: test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh (failed in all 4 of my runs here, but research flagged it intermittent; treating research's classification as authoritative since a single dispatch's 4/4 is not strong evidence against low-frequency intermittency). NEW finding not in research: test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's baseline case ('baseline fixture is not clean') is ADDITIONALLY sensitive to real-time source-vs-deployed drift anywhere under agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ -- it failed in run1(instrumented) due to MY OWN uncommitted run-all.sh edit (confirmed by git-stashing the edit out and re-running the fixture check directly: PASS with 0 diff), and ALSO failed in true-baseline run2/run3 (run-all.sh unmodified, stashed) due to a TRANSIENT drift apparently caused by the concurrently-dispatched sibling task 262 editing/redeploying files in the same tree during that window (confirmed: 'diff -rq agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ .claude/scripts/' was clean immediately before and after those runs). This is environmental flakiness from concurrent multi-task orchestration, not a code regression from this task, and not one of the 5 known pre-existing failures. Must be watched for (and not misattributed) during Phase 6's repeated-run flakiness gate.
